title: Tiger and sheep
prompt: One hundred tigers and one sheep are placed on a magic island with unlimited grass. Tigers can eat grass to survive, but they would much rather eat the sheep.

The rules: only one tiger can eat the sheep at a time, and any tiger that eats the sheep immediately becomes a sheep itself — vulnerable to being eaten by the others. All tigers are perfectly rational and value survival above all else.
hints: Start with 1 tiger. It eats the sheep immediately — no risk. Now try 2 tigers.
With 2 tigers: if tiger A eats the sheep, it becomes a sheep, and tiger B eats it. So neither tiger acts. Work through 3 and 4.
Look for a pattern in odd vs. even numbers of tigers.
solution_lede:
Like most recursive puzzles, this one dissolves once you start small.

1 tiger: eats the sheep — no risk. 2 tigers: eating converts you to a sheep, which the remaining tiger immediately eats. Neither acts; sheep survives. 3 tigers: eating converts you to a sheep in a 2-tiger world, where the sheep is safe — so you survive. The first rational tiger eats. 4 tigers: eating converts you to a sheep in a 3-tiger world, where the sheep gets eaten — you die. Nobody acts.

The pattern is clear: odd number of tigers → sheep gets eaten; even → sheep is safe. With 100 tigers (even), no tiger will make the first move.

solution_steps.body: n=1: tiger eats the sheep freely.
n=2: eating converts you to a sheep in a 1-tiger world. You get eaten. Neither tiger acts.
n=3: eating converts you to a sheep in a 2-tiger world — where the sheep is safe. You survive. First tiger eats.
Pattern: even → sheep safe, odd → sheep eaten. n=100 is even. The sheep is never eaten.
